subject: spanish
title: Voz Pasiva y Estilo Indirecto
welcome_lead: Passive voice and reported speech diversify Spanish. Ser vs estar shapes meaning.
meta_desc: Spanish grammar: passive voice, reported speech, gerund.
final_note: Cambiar la voz cambia la perspectiva.

walkthroughs.body_html: El libro fue escrito por Cervantes. Reflexive passive is common: Se hablan varios idiomas.
Present > imperfect. Dice que viene > Dijo que venia. Future > conditional.
Estudiando, aprendo. Continuous: estoy estudiando. Spanish gerund is more restricted than English -ing.

mcqs.q: Which preposition introduces the agent in passive?
Why does 'Me gusta el chocolate' literally translate as 'Chocolate is pleasing to me'?
options: It is a typo for 'Yo gusto'.
Gustar works backwards - the thing liked is the subject, the person is the indirect object.
Gustar means 'to like' and works exactly like English.
Tú is informal, tu is formal.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between 'tu' and 'tú'?
options: They are identical with optional accent.
Tú is informal, tu is formal.

mcqs.q: In Spain, how do you address a group of friends informally?
options: It is a typo for 'Yo gusto'.
